item.description:
Snap to the screen's edges

  • Drag to Snap has a new Screen edges mode. Drag a window into a corner for a quarter of the screen, against a side for half, to the top for the whole screen, or to the bottom for the third under the pointer. On a portrait screen, the sides give thirds and the bottom the lower half.
  • Guides along the screen's edges show where each zone is while you drag, and light up under the pointer.
  • Choose it in Settings → Mouse → Snap by. Layout mode works just as before. New installs start with drag to snap on, in Screen edges mode.
  • The menu now warns when macOS's own tiling is on, since it fights drag to snap, and links straight to the setting.

Center and Restore

  • Center Window (⌃⌥C) moves the front window to the middle of the screen, keeping its size.
  • Restore Window (⌃⌥⌫) puts a window back how it was before WindowSmith moved it. With drag to snap on, dragging a snapped window away does the same.
  • Both are also buttons in the menu, under Quick Snap.

Shortcuts and Settings

  • WindowSmith's shortcuts now belong to it alone, so a press no longer also reaches the app in front.
  • Settings is now in four tabs: General, Shortcuts, Mouse and My Layouts. It reopens on the tab you last used.
  • After saving a layout, you can put it on a shortcut in one click.
  • If macOS takes away WindowSmith's Accessibility access, Settings says so and offers a fix.

Green button

  • Quitting WindowSmith now gives Apple's green-button menu back, and opening it hides Apple's menu again.
